subject: Mental Models
title: Seeing Around Corners
description: A quick, practical guide to Seeing Around Corners.

hook.text: In 2007 a few investors predicted the housing crash while thousands of experts missed it entirely.

buildup.text: The investors used second-order thinking. They asked: what happens next after everyone buys risky mortgages?

discovery.text: Most people think one step ahead. Mental models let you think two or three steps into the future.

twist.text: You don't need a crystal ball. Combining a few models often reveals what single-track thinking misses.

climax.text: Second-order thinkers ask: and then what? That single question separates forecasters from guessers.

punchline.text: First-order thinking reacts. Second-order thinking anticipates.

quiz.question: What distinguishes second-order thinking from first-order thinking?
options: It asks 'and then what?' to think multiple steps ahead
